quarterly_data.quarter: Sumitomo Metal Mining annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: FY ended March 2026 (IFRS, annual securities report): net sales JPY 1,741,586 million (+9.3%), profit before tax JPY 255,680 million (+714.7%), profit attributable to owners of the parent JPY 176,290 million (+969.3%). Segments (including inter-segment sales): Resources net sales JPY 302,577 million (+43.6%), segment profit JPY 167,831 million (+64.8%) on higher copper and gold prices and smooth operation of the Cote gold mine; Smelting & Refining net sales JPY 1,350,058 million (+9.7%), segment profit JPY 91,593 million (prior year a loss of JPY 7,147 million after an impairment at an overseas nickel smelting subsidiary), despite worse copper concentrate purchase terms; Materials net sales JPY 284,509 million (down 4.0%), segment profit JPY 15,290 million (prior year a loss of JPY 54,231 million after a battery-materials impairment). Average prices: copper US$10,816/t (US$9,370), nickel US$7.08/lb (US$7.51), gold US$3,939.1/toz (US$2,584.7); JPY 150.78/US$ (152.58). The report states copper and gold both hit record highs in January 2026, copper on demand growth from AI-related investment and tight copper ore supply.
quarterly_data.figure: Net sales JPY 1,741,586 million (+9.3%); Materials segment profit JPY 15,290 million (loss of JPY 54,231 million a year earlier)

quarterly_data.quarter: Sumitomo Metal Mining annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Materials business, FY ended March 2026 (management's analysis, annual securities report): automotive battery-material demand grew only moderately as EV / hybrid demand varied by country and region, while for electronic-component materials, demand for data-center materials and semiconductor-related demand led the market and demand was on a gradual recovery trend; Materials segment profit improved, beyond the absence of the prior year's battery-materials impairment, on higher profit in materials for communication devices. In the functional-materials business, demand for data-center-related electronic-component materials and for catalysts stayed firm. Management expects demand growth from the spread of generative AI and other advanced technologies and from growing data-center use, but says the uncertain world economy leaves a risk that market growth slows.

quarterly_data.quarter: Sumitomo Metal Mining annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Production, FY ended March 2026 (annual securities report; includes toll processing): electrolytic copper 412,591 t (442,960 t a year earlier), gold 14,261 kg (18,709 kg), electrolytic nickel 66,155 t (60,108 t; a record high), ferronickel 4,800 t (3,317 t). Copper output and sales fell because of a scheduled major furnace overhaul at the Toyo copper smelter. Mines: Hishikari gold sales 3.5 t as planned; Morenci copper mine (US) 314 kt (25.0% attributable); Cerro Verde (Peru) 391 kt on lower feed grade (16.8%); Quebrada Blanca (Chile) 183 kt, down on a temporary tailings-facility capacity constraint (25.0%); Cote gold mine (Canada) 12.4 t, above plan (30.0%). Coral Bay Nickel output was slightly lower and Taganito HPAL Nickel output higher year on year.
quarterly_data.figure: Electrolytic nickel 66,155 t (record); electrolytic copper 412,591 t; gold 14,261 kg

quarterly_data.quarter: Sumitomo Metal Mining annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Medium-Term Management Plan 2027 (FY2025-FY2027) strategy and first-year progress (annual securities report): bring the Quebrada Blanca copper mine and the Cote gold mine to full strength (Quebrada Blanca Phase 2, 25% owned, met all project-finance completion conditions in April 2025; Cote continued commercial production); rebuild the battery-materials business (restructuring to fit its scale, productivity and cost cuts, continued development of all-solid-state / Ni-based next-generation and LFP battery materials); ferronickel: a new nickel matte furnace to strengthen its nickel supply chain; LT/LN (lithium tantalate / niobate crystal) business: consolidation of production sites and wider applications; growth projects: Kalgoorlie Nickel Project Goongarrie Hub (Australia), the Winu copper-gold project (Australia; agreement signed to acquire 30% of Rio Tinto's interest), lithium-ion battery recycling plant construction and start-up as planned, sales expansion of the 8-inch bonded SiC substrate SiCkrest and of the SiC polycrystal used as its bonded support substrate, and the near-infrared absorbing material SOLAMENT entering agriculture. The new Niihama battery-materials plant (Ehime), built for capacity expansion, was completed with a ceremony in May 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: 8-inch SiCkrest sales expansion; Winu 30% interest agreement; Niihama battery-materials plant completed May 2025

quarterly_data.quarter: Sumitomo Metal Mining annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management's view of the business environment (annual securities report; the copper TC/RC, battery-materials and functional-materials points are the medium-term environment the company set out when drawing up Medium-Term Management Plan 2027): nickel is expected to stay oversupplied but improve gradually as demand rises slowly while production increases, mainly in Indonesia, are constrained; copper is expected to be oversupplied as uncertainty from the Middle East and national policies dampens demand; copper smelting margins (TC/RC) are assumed to recover only after 2030; battery materials face fast-changing conditions and fiercer price and technology competition from slower EV demand and the rise of overseas battery makers; for functional materials the outlook is uncertain amid slower EV demand, no growth driver other than generative AI and the spread of bloc economies.

quarterly_data.quarter: Sumitomo Metal Mining annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: R&D, FY ended March 2026 (annual securities report): R&D expense JPY 9,050 million (Resources JPY 357 million, Smelting & Refining JPY 2,307 million, Materials JPY 5,953 million). Materials: developed a fine copper powder (oxidation resistant, low-temperature sintering, uniform particle size) added to a thick-film conductive ink for printed electronics; the report says the powder is highly rated for its fit with SiC and other power-semiconductor applications; exhibits its iron-gallium (Fe-Ga) magnetostrictive single crystal for energy harvesting; is moving newly developed lithium nickelate cathode materials into mass production and developing next-generation high-performance nickel cathodes and all-solid-state battery cathodes, with the Battery Research Institute's second development building (pilot equipment for medium-scale verification) completed in December. Smelting & Refining: with Kanto Denka Kogyo it established a technology that turns slag recovered in the pyrometallurgical step into high-purity lithium compounds reusable for battery materials (company says a world first); cathode material made with recycled lithium performed on par with natural-resource material, evaluation at customers of cathodes made entirely from recycled nickel, cobalt and lithium is planned, and demonstration toward commercialization in 2026 is under way as a NEDO Green Innovation Fund project. Resources: a direct lithium extraction pilot test in Antofagasta, Chile.
